answer: Coordination-Debt Pricing. Each new identity must complete a voyage of N verified interactions before its votes count, and a shared jade ledger records the coordination load every identity imposes on peers. Identities that join late or cluster tightly pay escalating coordination rents, scaled by how much shared trellis capacity their actions consume. An attacker running k synthetic identities must front real work and rent for all k before any influence accrues, making each marginal identity strictly costlier than the last.
